text:
Crystalline inflammatory disease, due to monosodium urate monohydrate
crystals deposition in joints and tissues. Due either to excessive uric acid
production from intrinsic purine metabolism or extrinsic (dietary). Also due to
decrease renal excretion of uric acid and resultant accumulation in the blood.
Commonly seen in males (40 years and above) and post-menopausal females.
Four major types:
- Asymptomatic
- Acute
- Inter critical
- Chronic tophaceous
It could be either primary (no identifiable cause) or secondary. Secondary
causes: dehydration, fasting, renal impairment, hypertension, malignancies
such as lymphoma, leukaemia, psoriasis, sickle cell disease, use of cytotoxic
agents, excessive alcohol intake especially beer
Low dose aspirin, Drugs such as pyrazinamide, diuretics.
